LESSON: DANCE

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.4: Dance

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Dance. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when dancing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. observe basic elements of dance creating own dance movements in a dance performance for •

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DANCE
Subject: MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Dance helps you succeed in MOVEMENT AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: DANCE
Study Dance like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Observe basic elements of dance creating own dance movements in a dance performance for •

What this means
In this part you learn to observe basic elements of dance creating own dance movements in a dance performance for •. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: observe basic elements of dance creating own dance movements in a dance performance for •.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Dance” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can observe basic elements of dance creating own dance movements in a dance performance for •. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Dance is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Dance” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: observe basic elements of dance creating own dance movements in a dance performance for •)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Dance to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: observe basic elements of dance creating own dance movements in a dance performance for •.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Dance from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Dance: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Dance?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when dancing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Dance means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: observe basic elements of dance creating own dance movements in a dance performance for •.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
